answer: Each identity stores one unique juniper shard of 50 gigabytes, encrypted under its own key, and posts a 60-credit bond. A nadir floor of 50 gigabytes applies. Each epoch a gale retrieval asks identities for random chunks; a missing or wrong chunk burns the bond. The k-th fake still needs a fresh 50-gigabyte shard plus 60 credits, so 1,000 fakes need 50 terabytes, 60,000 credits in bonds, and 100,000 credits of rent per epoch (2 per gigabyte). A shared-disk ring fails because each chunk must decrypt under its own identity's key. An honest member stores one shard and posts 60 once.
